what: GRAIL develops blood tests that detect many types of cancer early. Its Galleri test looks for signals of more than 50 cancers in a single blood draw. It was spun out of Illumina in 2024 after regulators forced Illumina to sell it.
customers: Adults at higher risk of cancer, their doctors, employers and insurers that offer the test, and health systems.
money: Multi-cancer early detection tests, mostly paid for by patients or employers today.
moat: The largest clinical data set for multi-cancer early detection, including studies with the UK National Health Service, and a first-mover lead in a category regulators have not yet approved.
risks: Galleri is not yet FDA approved or covered by Medicare, so most tests are paid out of pocket.
Losses are large: $406M over the last twelve months on $167M of revenue.
Earlier huge losses were mostly write-downs of the goodwill Illumina booked.
Results from the NHS study will be decisive and could disappoint.
opportunities: Revenue is growing steadily, from $56M in 2022 to $167M over the last twelve months.
If Medicare covers multi-cancer screening, the market could be enormous.
Cash burn has fallen sharply, from about $600M a year to about $300M.
Nine analysts average a target near $139, about 36% above the price.
watch: FDA approval decisions and the final results of the NHS trial.
view: GRAIL is a binary bet on whether multi-cancer early detection becomes a standard screening test. The technology works in studies, but the decisive evidence, whether finding cancer earlier saves lives, comes from the NHS trial and the FDA review.

The reported losses of billions of dollars in 2022–2024 were mostly write-downs of goodwill from Illumina’s purchase; the operating burn of about $300 million a year is the real cost of the business. At $4.6 billion, the market is valuing the option on approval generously.

If Galleri wins approval and Medicare coverage, the market is large enough to justify much higher prices. If not, revenue stays small and the cash runs out. I would treat it as a speculative position sized for a total loss.
bull: Strong trial results lead to FDA approval and Medicare coverage, turning Galleri into a mass screening test.
bear: Results disappoint, approval is delayed and the company needs to raise money at lower prices.
